title: Career Roadmap: Merchandise Planner
summary: A Merchandise Planner ensures that the right products are available, in the right quantities, at the right locations and at the right time. The role combines fashion and consumer understanding with sales forecasting, inventory management, budgeting and data analysis.

blocks.text: Merchandise Planner

blocks.label: Academic pathway
blocks.text: B.FTech / B.Des Fashion – Fashion Business / Retail Management

A Merchandise Planner ensures that the right products are available, in the right quantities, at the right locations and at the right time. The role combines fashion and consumer understanding with sales forecasting, inventory management, budgeting and data analysis.

In fashion retail, merchandise planners help determine what a brand should buy, how much stock it needs, when products should arrive and how inventory should be distributed across stores and online channels. They work closely with buying, merchandising, sourcing, finance, supply chain and retail teams.
This career is particularly suitable for students who enjoy fashion and retail but also have an interest in numbers, business decisions, spreadsheets and analytical problem-solving.
Sales forecasting
Estimate future sales by product, category, season, store and channel using historical performance and market signals.
Inventory planning
Balance stock availability with demand, avoiding unnecessary excess inventory and missed sales from stockouts.
Financial and assortment planning
Plan sales, markdowns, margins, budgets, stock cover and product-category performance to support retail profitability.
Fashion Merchandise Planner
Plans seasonal clothing collections, stock quantities, size distributions and sales targets for fashion categories.
Inventory Planner
Monitors stock levels, replenishment, inventory ageing, stock cover and product availability across locations.
Assortment Planner
Determines the product mix, price points, colour options, sizes and categories that best serve target customers.
Retail Planning Analyst
Uses sales data, profitability measures and forecasts to support buying, allocation and business planning decisions.
E-commerce Merchandise Planner
Plans online product availability, inventory allocation, promotions and assortment performance across digital channels.

A fashion business or retail management qualification can provide a strong foundation. Students should add quantitative skills because merchandise planning is more analytical than many creative fashion roles.

Year 1
Understand fashion and business

items.text: Study fashion retail, consumer behaviour, economics and accounting fundamentals.
Learn Excel formulas, charts, tables and basic calculations.
Understand apparel categories, sizes, seasonal collections and pricing.
Track how product availability and pricing differ between retailers.

blocks.text: Year 2
Develop planning and inventory skills

items.text: Learn sales planning, assortment planning and inventory calculations.
Practise pivot tables, lookup functions and conditional formulas.
Calculate sell-through, gross margin, stock cover and markdown rates.
Build a sample category sales and inventory report.

blocks.text: Year 3
Learn forecasting and analytics

items.text: Build forecasts using historical sales and seasonal patterns.
Learn Power BI and introductory statistics.
Create stock-allocation and replenishment models.
Seek internships in merchandise planning, retail analytics or buying operations.

blocks.text: Final year
Prepare for industry roles

items.text: Complete an end-to-end merchandise planning case study.
Prepare a seasonal sales budget and stock plan.
Explain how you would respond to slow-moving products and stockouts.
Build a portfolio of planning spreadsheets, dashboards and business recommendations.

blocks.text: Important retail calculations

rows.text: How much of the available or received stock has sold, using a consistently defined denominator
Sales revenue less cost of goods sold, expressed in value or as a percentage
How long current inventory may last at an assumed rate of sales
How frequently inventory is sold and replenished over a period
Difference between planned and actual sales or inventory results
Reduction from original price or the proportion of sales affected by markdowns, depending on the definition used

blocks.text: Employers need evidence that a candidate can make sound commercial decisions, not just create attractive reports.

blocks.label: Project 1
blocks.text: Seasonal merchandise plan
Create a category-level sales budget with monthly targets, assumptions, planned inventory and a variance-tracking sheet. Label any simulated figures clearly.

blocks.label: Project 2
blocks.text: Inventory and replenishment analysis
Use sample data to identify stockouts, excess inventory, slow-moving items and products that may need replenishment.

blocks.label: Project 3
blocks.text: Sales forecasting dashboard
Build an Excel or Power BI dashboard comparing actual sales with forecasts by category, month, store or product group.

blocks.label: Project 4
blocks.text: Open-to-buy and markdown plan
Create a simplified buying budget, estimate planned purchases and propose markdown actions for slow-selling stock.

blocks.label: Project 5
blocks.text: Assortment and size-curve analysis
Compare product categories, price bands, colours and sizes to propose a balanced assortment for a hypothetical fashion retailer.

For each project, include the business question, data definitions, assumptions, calculations, visualisations, recommendation and limitations. Use public or simulated datasets responsibly and never disclose confidential company information.
Look for roles that expose students to sales data, stock planning, retail operations and product performance.

By graduation, an aspiring Merchandise Planner should aim to have:

items.text: A relevant fashion business, retail management or fashion technology qualification.
Strong Excel skills and working knowledge of retail planning metrics.
Practical experience with sales forecasting and inventory planning.
A portfolio containing merchandise plans, dashboards and assortment analysis.
Understanding of how stock availability, pricing and markdowns influence profitability.
Experience through an internship, simulated retail case study or industry project.
The ability to communicate analytical findings and recommend commercial actions.

blocks.label: Final recommendation
blocks.text: Build a profile that combines fashion retail knowledge, quantitative analysis and commercial decision-making. A graduate who can forecast demand, explain inventory risks and propose practical buying or replenishment actions will be better prepared for merchandise planning roles.
